text:
Noah Cates is the kind of player whose value doesn't show up in a points column, and this season's line (two goals, five points in 20 games) won't change anyone's mind. The Stillwater kid who went in the fifth round has carved out a real NHL job anyway, and the reason is defence.

Evolving-Hockey had him at 2.1 wins above replacement last season, 47th among 401 forwards, with most of it coming on the penalty kill, and opponents got noticeably fewer good chances with him out there (97th percentile). It also says plainly that offence isn't his game. This season fits the pattern in a good way: the Flyers have taken 52% of the expected goals at five on five with him on the ice (the quality of chances), almost 11 points better than when he sits, on a team that has struggled to control games. His finishing is normal and his teammates have been a little unlucky around him. Watch the minutes, about 13 a night: the more Philadelphia trusts him against top lines, the more that defensive value matters.
